content: Upon discharge, it is essential to provide comprehensive education on diabetes self-management. This education should include detailed training on how to recognize the symptoms of hyperglycemia, such as excessive thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue, as well as the symptoms of hypoglycemia, such as shakiness, confusion, and sweating. Patients should also receive specific dietary guidance tailored to their condition, emphasizing the importance of balanced meals and carbohydrate monitoring. Additionally, they must be instructed on the proper use of essential diabetes management tools, including insulin pens, syringes, and blood glucose meters, ensuring they are confident in their ability to use these devices correctly and safely.
